quotes.quote: Incumbents can’t simply tear down their UIs and business models to pivot
categories that have historically monetized gatekept institutional knowledge will be most susceptible
Law is obviously at risk (Harvey and Legora are exploding)

rationale: The post makes a specific structural claim about which incumbents agents will displace and why (inability to pivot UIs and business models), which no existing thesis covers.

quotes.quote: you can basically get fee-free, liquid, and leverageable frontier-ish exposure with copper/power/etc today and basically no one cares
if you really want just a simple way to bet on AI
just bet on energy

rationale: Both the post and the quoted Fred Wilson clip argue that energy and commodities are the simple way to bet on AI.

quotes.quote: Data centres account for around one-tenth of global electricity demand growth to 2030, less than the share from industrial motors, air conditioning in homes and offices, or electric vehicles.

rationale: The power leg works for US-exposed power names, not for global energy as a whole.

quotes.quote: In the United States, data centres account for nearly half of electricity demand growth between now and 2030.
Data centre electricity consumption is set to more than double to around 945 TWh by 2030.

rationale: AI is a material driver of US power demand growth, the market most US power equities sell into.

quotes.quote: data centers consumed about 4.4% of total U.S. electricity in 2023 and are expected to consume approximately 6.7 to 12% of total U.S. electricity by 2028

rationale: A doubling-to-tripling of the US data-centre share is material for US power markets.

quotes.quote: 2% for copper
the absolute volumes in 2030 still reach 512 kilotonnes (kt) of copper

rationale: At ~2% of demand, AI is not what sets the copper price, so copper is weak AI exposure.

quotes.quote: copper demand from the sector will average around 400,000 tonnes annually over the next decade, peaking at 572,000 tonnes in 2028
potentially pushing the supply shortfall to 6 million tonnes by 2035

rationale: AI adds marginal tonnes to a market BNEF sees as structurally short; the tightness comes mostly from elsewhere.

quotes.quote: approximately 80% are traditional customers and 20% are for
data center orders to over $5 billion in the first half of 2026, more than double full-year

rationale: Grid and turbine equipment is real but partial AI exposure: data centers are a minority of the gas-turbine book.

quotes.quote: Constellation, for example, has signed a power agreement with Microsoft to restart the Three Mile Island nuclear plant
Talen is powering an Amazon data center with electricity from the nearby Susquehanna nuclear plant.

rationale: Independent power producers have contracted, direct AI revenue, making them the most direct liquid power expression.

quotes.quote: Vistra closed nearly 30% lower, erasing its gains for 2025. Constellation Energy, Talen Energy and GE Vernova tumbled more than 20%

rationale: AI power equities already trade as high-beta AI proxies, so the 'overlooked' part of the thesis fails for them.

quotes.quote: the global refined copper market would remain in surplus through 2027, with it widening from about 104 000 metric tons in 2026 to 368 000 metric tons in 2027

rationale: Near term the copper market is not supply-constrained, so AI demand need not translate into copper price.

quotes.quote: electricity demand from data centres is 20% lower in 2035 than in the Base Case
spans from 700 to 1 700 TWh

rationale: Efficiency gains are a quantified, plausible path to the kill criterion for the power leg.
